title: Item
description: A corpus item. An 'archetype' is a recurring interview pattern attested by sources; an 'instance' is a concrete, gradeable problem written against an archetype. Statements are ALWAYS original prose — sources justify that the pattern is real, they are never copied from.

modality.description: Which interview runtime and grader handles this item.

archetype_id.description: Required on instances: the archetype this problem realizes. Null on archetypes.

statement_md.description: ORIGINAL prose, Markdown. The validator rejects statements with high n-gram overlap against any cited source.

concepts.description: Every concept this item produces evidence for.

primary_concept.description: The one concept this item is chiefly a measurement of. Must appear in `concepts`.

elo.description: Seed rating. Updated from real outcomes once the item has been attempted — the corpus value is only a prior.

sources.description: At least two INDEPENDENT sources. This is the evidence-density signal that ranks archetypes; it is not a citation for copied text.

evidence.description: Why this source attests the archetype is really asked. Paraphrase, not a quoted problem statement.

hints.description: Graduated hints, least to most revealing. Every hint the interviewer reveals is recorded and reduces the score.

follow_ups.description: Pressure-test questions the interviewer may ask once the main problem lands.

entrypoint.description: Function name the candidate must implement.

reference_solutions.description: Per-language reference implementation. CI asserts each one passes every test.

complexity_target.description: e.g. 'O(n)'. The complexity probe fits the growth curve against this. Inert without `complexity_probe`, which is what actually supplies inputs of size n.

complexity_probe.description: How to build an input of size n. Without this the probe cannot run at all: the fixed `input` arrays in `tests` cannot be grown, so `complexity_target` alone is unenforceable.

generator.description: Python source defining make_input(n) -> list of positional args for the entrypoint. Must be deterministic (seed any randomness) so a verdict is reproducible.

sizes.description: Ascending n values. Pick them so the largest run clears ~0.2ms, below which interpreter noise dominates and the probe reports inconclusive.

repeats.description: Runs per size; the minimum is taken, which rejects scheduling noise better than a mean does.

exact.description: Symbolic form, checked with sympy equivalence — so 1/3, 0.333..., and 2/6 all pass.

accept_forms.description: Additional literal forms to accept, for answers sympy cannot normalize.

reasoning_rubric.description: A correct number with wrong reasoning is not a pass in a real quant interview. This grades the derivation.

concept.description: Concept this criterion writes evidence against. Defaults to the item's primary_concept.

levels.description: Score anchors, so the LLM grader has something concrete to match against instead of a vibe.
